title: Dynamic Node Creation in Backpropagation Networks
summary: Introduces Dynamic Node Creation, a constructive approach in which a backpropagation network can add hidden units during training instead of fixing hidden-layer size in advance; inspected private-PDF snippets support a plateau/flatness trigger on the average squared-error curve.
growth_mechanism: Adds hidden nodes one at a time during backpropagation training; inspected private-PDF snippets say a new hidden node is triggered when flattening of the average squared-error curve is detected, after which regular backpropagation continues until the desired mapping is learned or another node is needed.
notes: Seed bibliography item verified against Crossref for the Connection Science article. Semantic Scholar also indexes a 1989 IJCNN version with DOI 10.1109/IJCNN.1989.118509. Automated review draft improved with Crossref API, DOI landing page, Semantic Scholar metadata, targeted web search, and a verified private PDF path. On 2026-07-15, lightweight PDF byte/Flate-string inspection supported cautious notes that DNC adds hidden nodes one at a time, uses flattening of the average squared-error curve as the addition trigger, and resumes regular backpropagation after node growth; exact formulae, parameter definitions, and experiment conclusions still need human full-text verification. Synthesis note: post-growth stabilization remains a comparison axis, but this pass found no evidence that DNC freezes installed features in the Cascade-Correlation sense.

title: The Cascade-Correlation Learning Architecture
summary: Introduces a supervised constructive architecture that starts minimal, trains candidate units to correlate with residual error, installs the best unit, freezes it, and repeats.
growth_mechanism: Candidate hidden units compete by correlation with residual error; the best unit is installed and its incoming weights are frozen.
notes: Primary anchor paper for early site demos. Proceedings/Semantic Scholar index it under NeurIPS 1989, while this repository keeps the established 1990 ID pending a human bibliographic cleanup pass. On 2026-07-16, the private library PDF path was verified under pdfs/Constructive and the asset record was updated from located to collected; extraction tooling was still unavailable, and embedded PDF metadata was generic conversion metadata rather than article-specific bibliographic evidence.

title: Constructive Learning of Recurrent Neural Networks: Limitations of Recurrent Cascade Correlation and a Simple Solution
summary: Analyzes recurrent cascade-correlation, proves topology-driven representational limitations for some finite-state automata, and sketches a constructive fully recurrent alternative that adds neurons during training.
growth_mechanism: Constructively adds neurons during recurrent-network training while preserving a fully recurrent structure, proposed as an alternative to recurrent cascade-correlation's restrictive topology.
notes: Metadata verified against IEEE Xplore and Penn State Pure pages during the 2026-06-24 weekly discovery dry run. title: A Growing Neural Gas Network Learns Topologies
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 7
summary: Introduces Growing Neural Gas: moving input-space prototypes, competitive-Hebbian edges with local aging, and periodic insertion directed by accumulated squared-distance error.

title: Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning for NLP
summary: Introduces bottleneck adapter modules: small down-project/nonlinearity/up-project blocks inserted twice per Transformer layer, trained per task while the original network stays fixed.
growth_mechanism: New layers are added inside each Transformer block — after the multi-head-attention output projection and after the feed-forward sub-layer — each projecting d features down to m, applying a nonlinearity, projecting back to d, with an internal skip connection; 2md+d+m parameters per adapter. Near-zero initialization makes each adapter an approximate identity at the start of training.
notes: Bibliographic fields and mechanism quotes were read from the public arXiv abstract page and the ar5iv HTML rendering of the paper on 2026-09-05. No PDF or extracted text was copied into Git. Not human-reviewed.

title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
summary: Freezes the pre-trained weights and learns a low-rank update BA alongside each adapted matrix, so the trainable parameter count drops sharply and the delta can be merged back into the base weights before inference.
growth_mechanism: For a frozen weight matrix W0, the forward pass becomes h = W0x + BAx with B in R^{d x r}, A in R^{r x k} and r much smaller than min(d,k); A is initialized from a random Gaussian and B is initialized to zero, so the delta starts at exactly zero, and the delta output is scaled by alpha/r. In the paper's Transformer experiments only attention weights are adapted (Wq and Wv), with MLP modules frozen.
notes: Bibliographic fields and mechanism quotes were read from the public arXiv abstract page and the ar5iv HTML rendering on 2026-09-05. No PDF or extracted text was copied into Git. Not human-reviewed.

title: Mixture of LoRA Experts
summary: Composes several already-trained LoRAs by learning a gating function over them instead of arithmetically merging them, keeping both the base model and every LoRA frozen.
growth_mechanism: Each layer of each trained LoRA is treated as a distinct expert, and a learnable gating function inside each layer produces softmax weights over the concatenated expert outputs. Two losses give the hierarchical control: a balancing loss that is minimized under balanced dispatching, and a domain-specific loss. Only the gating parameters are optimized; all trained LoRAs and the pre-trained model are frozen. At inference, undesired LoRAs can be masked out and the remaining gate weights renormalized proportionally.
notes: Bibliographic fields and mechanism quotes were read from the public arXiv abstract page and the ar5iv HTML rendering on 2026-09-05. No PDF or extracted text was copied into Git. Not human-reviewed.
